question: Define \([a,b,c]\) to mean \(\frac{a+b}{c},\) where \(c\ne0.\) What is the value of \[ [[60,30,90],[2,1,3],[10,5,15]]? \]
solution:
The entries of the outer bracket are themselves bracket values, so first apply the given rule to the three inner brackets:
\[
[60,30,90]=\frac{60+30}{90}=1,
\]
\[
[2,1,3]=\frac{2+1}{3}=1,
\]
\[
[10,5,15]=\frac{10+5}{15}=1.
\]
The divisors \(90\), \(3\), and \(15\) are all nonzero. Substituting these three results into the outer bracket gives
\[
[1,1,1]=\frac{1+1}{1}=\boxed{2}.
\]
Its divisor is also nonzero, so the expression is defined. The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
